messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: hosted-api gpu-pool-eu-west-2 queue depth rising above 18k, p95=12.4s p99=38.1s, errors=2.3% -> creating incident (sev=2) :rotating_light:
jay: I’m oncall — joining. seeing heavy traffic from a few clients? any early bleachers?
maya: Confirmed spike at 08:12 UTC. Queue ingestion rate ~3.2k req/s vs baseline 450 req/s. Looks like autoscaler tried to provision but kept failing.
chris: Checking provisioner logs now. Posting relevant tail:```2026-01-14T08:12:30Z provisioner: create_instance failed: API error: InsufficientInstanceCapacity: Could not fulfill request for p4d.xlarge in eu-west-2
2026-01-14T08:12:31Z autoscaler: attempt=4 delay=12s reason=quotaExceeded provider=cloud-api code=QuotaExceeded
2026-01-14T08:12:45Z pool-manager: thin-provision pool entering throttle-shim state```
anita: autoscaler shows repeated 429 from cloud provider at the same window; quotaExceeded on GPU SKU and a subsequent rate-limited create loop. Looks like we hit regional soft-limits plus an internal backoff bug that prevented fallback to lower-spec instances.
jay: Customer impact? any 5xxs surfacing to customers or timeouts?
ellie: CS queue: multiple customers reported timeouts and slow responses for embeddings and chat — one high-volume customer (acme-inc) reports 50% error spike. We've flagged them and started mitigation comms.
maya: Observing our hosted front-end started shedding 10% of requests at 08:15 to protect latency SLOs. That triggered routed fallback but fallback models saturated too.
jorge: Escalating to infra lead. If we can’t get more GPUs, we should route heavy callers to dedicated or apply adaptive throttles.
chris: Attempting manual pool resize to smaller GPU family (a100->t4 mixture) but need to update instance type mapping; will try command:```provisioner scale --pool hosted-eu-w-2 --target-instances 24 --instance-types p4d,a100,t4```
anita: Heads up — runtime currently doesn't support automatic model-quantization fallback for chat endpoints; enabling quantized variant requires a rollout which takes ~3m. Could help throughput if we can swap models.
jay: Execute immediate mitigations: 1) block top noisy API keys (rate-limit to 50r/s) 2) enable model-quantized flag on canary for 10% of traffic 3) route non-critical embeddings to dedicated backlog bucket 4) open cloud support ticket for replenish capacity.
ellie: Notifying affected customers: emailed top-10 customers with note that we're investigating GPU capacity issues and applying mitigations; they've escalated a priority ticket for acme-inc.
maya: Doing 1) now — applying rate-limit policy for the top 8 keys:```/api/v1/admin/rate_limits apply --keys k_123,k_456 --limit 50```
chris: Manual resize started -> cloud returned: `create_instances: 10/24 succeeded, 14 failed: InsufficientInstanceCapacity` — still not enough. Also seeing provider returning 429s on quota check.
jorge: Can we fallback to lower-memory variants and accept slightly longer latency but reduced OOM? If runtime can accept t4 it might at least relieve backlog.
anita: Started canary model-swap to quantized-v2 on one router (10% traffic). Observed immediate CPU-side drop in token compute and drop in per-token cost. Early metrics: p95 for canary slice dropped from 11s -> 6.8s.
jay: Good. Keep rolling to 30% if stable and no correctness regressions. Maya, coordinate with CS for customer-facing status update.
maya: Posted status update in status.redwood.com (incident created) and sent short customer note: "We're experiencing GPU capacity constraints in EU region causing elevated latency and some timeouts. We're applying throttles and fallbacks; updates in 15m."
ellie: Acme-inc asks for ETA. We told them 30-60m pending cloud quota lifts or manual routing. They asked for a refund credit if SLA violated. Logging request.
chris: Found an autoscaler bug — when quotaExceeded occurs it stops trying other instance families because of an early return in the loop. Opening PR to change behavior but won't ship in this window. Patch link: https://git.internal/redwood/provisioner/pulls/1984
anita: Short-term fix: enable cross-family fallback in the pool manager via feature flag (hot toggle). Doing it now:```curl -X POST https://config.internal/flags -d '{"flag":"allow_cross_family_fallback","value":true}'```
chris: Cross-family fallback toggled. Immediately seeing more t4 instance creations succeed. Pool capacity improving.
maya: Queue depth trending down from 18k -> 9.3k in last 7m. p95 down to 9.2s, p99 21.0s. Error rate slipping but still elevated at 1.1%.
jay: OK — maintain rate limits on noisy keys and continue canary to 30%. Hold on full rollout until we validate output quality for top 5 clients.
jorge: Ops checklist: 1) cloud support ticket opened (ID: CS-78321) 2) emergency quota request submitted 3) temporary routing to dedicated enabled for partner accounts 4) post-incident blameless: schedule root-cause meeting tomorrow
ellie: CS filed chargeback & credit request for acme-inc; they want 24h of usage credit if SLA breached. We already logged incident severity as sev2.
anita: Monitoring: adding extra eval rollups for canary responses vs baseline to watch for regressions. Doing periodic checks on similarity and hallucination metrics.
chris: Provisioner backlog cleared almost fully; we have 20/24 target instances now in mixed families. Remaining failures are sporadic insufficient capacity for large p4d requests.
maya: Traffic normalized to ~800 req/s from peak. We'll keep window open for 60 minutes before closing. Notifying oncall rotation for handoff at 09:15 UTC.
jay: Handoff to night shift: summary - spike caused regional GPU soft-limit + autoscaler early-return bug -> prevented cross-family fallback -> manual toggle fixed; mitigations: rate-limits on noisy keys, canary quantized model to 30%, routing non-critical embeddings to dedicated, cloud ticket open.
chris: Leaving a snippet of commands we used for runbook audit:```# look for quota errors
journalctl -u provisioner --since "-1h" | grep -i quota
# toggle fallback
curl -X POST https://config.internal/flags -d '{"flag":"allow_cross_family_fallback","value":true}'
# apply rate limits
/api/admin/rate_limits apply --keys <list> --limit 50
```
maya: Passing to jay for signoff handoff. I’ll stay on until rotation.
jay: Thanks all. Pager handoff notes attached to incident page. If cloud quota doesn't clear in 2h we'll enact long-lived mitigations (traffic shaping + dedicated invites). Closing open urgent tasks: manual toggles and customer comms  -> DONE. Will track next steps in postmortem. :white_check_mark:
